FR-01: The system shall provide a form on which a creator enters the category, title, planned duration, audio language, made-for-kids status and channel identifier of a planned video.
FR-02: The system shall offer category as a closed selection list of the standard YouTube content categories.
FR-03: The system shall accept intended publishing day and intended publishing hour as optional inputs and shall produce a forecast when either or both are omitted.
FR-04: The system shall not impute, default or average any omitted optional input; omitted inputs shall be carried through to the model as genuinely missing.
FR-05: The system shall accept titles containing Sinhala, Tamil or Latin script, or any mixture of them, without loss or corruption of characters.
FR-06: The system shall validate each input before submission, shall reject implausible values such as a non-positive duration, and shall explain in plain language what is wrong and how to correct it.
FR-07: The system shall retain the submitted inputs on the results view so that the creator can amend one value and resubmit without re-entering the rest.
FR-08: The system shall resolve a supplied channel URL or channel identifier to a channel record and retrieve its subscriber count, total view count, uploaded-video count and creation date.
FR-09: The system shall derive the channel's age in days from its creation date and the current date.
FR-10: The system shall not require the creator to enter any channel statistic manually.
FR-11: The system shall distinguish, in the message shown to the creator, between a channel that could not be found, a channel whose statistics are not publicly available, and a temporary failure of the external service.
FR-12: Where a channel's subscriber count is hidden by its owner, the system should still return a forecast, treating that input as missing.
FR-13: The system shall obtain, for each title, scores on a fixed common scale for urgency, emotional appeal, seriousness of register and curiosity gap.
FR-14: The system shall obtain all four scores from a single request per title.
FR-15: The system shall instruct the scoring service that titles may be multilingual and shall request scores reflecting a Sri Lankan reader's interpretation.
FR-16: The system shall validate that a returned score set is complete, numeric and within range, shall retry once on failure, and shall record the scores as unavailable thereafter.
FR-17: The system shall return a forecast when title tone scores are unavailable, treating them as missing inputs rather than failing the request.
FR-18: The system shall store one set of tone scores per video rather than one set per engagement observation.
FR-19: The system shall not compute, store, expose or act upon any score for divisiveness, communal or ethnic provocation, controversy potential, or misleading-claim strength.
FR-20: The system shall assemble the model's complete feature vector from the creator's inputs, the retrieved channel statistics and the title tone scores.
FR-21: The system shall apply the same transformations, in the same order, as were applied during training, using a single shared implementation rather than a reimplementation.
FR-22: The system shall obtain the categorical encoding from the frozen mapping published with the model and shall not recompute it at serving time.
FR-23: The system shall substitute the global average encoding for a category not present in the published mapping.
FR-24: The system shall present features to the model in the exact order recorded in the published feature-order artefact.
FR-25: The system shall expose no derived or encoded feature value to the creator.
FR-26: The system shall predict cumulative view counts at day 7, day 14, day 21 and day 30 after publication from pre-publication features alone.
FR-27: The system shall use no feature that could not be known before the video's publication timestamp.
FR-28: The system shall produce all four horizon predictions from a single trained model in a single inference.
FR-29: The system shall return predictions on the real view-count scale, having inverted any training-time transformation.
FR-30: The system shall produce a forecast when one or more inputs are missing, and shall indicate to the creator that the forecast was produced with incomplete information.
FR-31: The system shall round presented forecasts to a precision consistent with the model's measured accuracy.
FR-32: The system shall present the four horizon predictions as a single trajectory, both graphically and in plain-language prose.
FR-33: The system shall present the forecast without statistical notation or model terminology.
FR-34: The system shall state on the results view that the forecast is an estimate and shall identify, in general terms, the factors it cannot observe.
FR-35: The system shall indicate on the results view when the forecast was produced with one or more inputs missing.
FR-36: The system shall not display confidence intervals or prediction bands in this release.
FR-37: The system shall recommend a publishing day and time band for the selected category and channel size, and shall do so prominently when the creator has not specified them.
FR-38: The system shall indicate whether the planned duration falls within the range that has historically performed well for the selected category, and shall state that range.
FR-39: The system shall indicate whether short-form or standard uploads have historically performed better in the selected category for a channel of the given size.
FR-40: The system shall provide title framing guidance derived from the tone reading of the submitted title.
FR-41: The system shall accompany every recommendation with the historical pattern that supports it.
FR-42: The system shall present a recommendation only where the feature group underlying it has been shown by the ablation study to contribute measurably to accuracy.
FR-43: The system shall not generate guidance that advocates divisiveness, communal or ethnic provocation, or misleading claims.
FR-44: The system shall report the measured accuracy of the published model on held-out historical data, combined across horizons and separately per horizon.
FR-45: The system shall report the accuracy of the naive baseline alongside that of the model.
FR-46: The system shall state the size of the evaluation set and the date range it covers.
FR-47: The system shall explain the reported figures in plain language, including why longer horizons are less accurate.
FR-48: The system should allow a creator to supply the URL of a published video in order to record an actual outcome against a previously issued forecast.
FR-49: The system shall maintain a roster of Sri Lanka-based channels with their identifying details, category, subscriber count, creation date and uploads playlist reference.
FR-50: The system shall assign each channel a size tier computed relative to other channels in the same category, automatically at ingest.
FR-51: The system shall discover new videos by enumerating each rostered channel's uploads playlist using low-cost batched calls.
FR-52: The system shall not use search-class calls as a routine video-discovery mechanism.
FR-53: The system shall record, for every discovered video, its publication timestamp together with its descriptive metadata.
FR-54: The roster ingestion function shall be safely repeatable, updating existing channel records rather than duplicating or failing on them.
FR-55: The system shall poll the engagement statistics of every actively tracked video on a repeating unattended schedule.
FR-56: The system shall record, for each observation, the cumulative view, like and comment counts together with the observation time.
FR-57: The system shall compute a video's age from that video's own publication timestamp, and shall never derive it from the tracking start time or from a run sequence number.
FR-58: Every write to the engagement history shall be idempotent, such that repeated or retried runs neither duplicate observations nor fail.
FR-59: The system shall retain each video in the tracking set until it passes the end of its tracking window, after which it shall be marked complete and excluded from further polling.
FR-60: The system shall continue a run when an individual video is unavailable or returns an incomplete response, recording the condition rather than aborting the run.
FR-61: The system shall record the deviation between each observation and the exact horizon boundary, and shall mark whether that deviation is acceptable for use as a training label.
FR-62: Every external data API call shall be made through a single guard that records its cost against a daily ledger.
FR-63: The system shall permit search-class calls only when the remaining daily allowance exceeds a configured safety margin.
FR-64: The system shall halt collection cleanly and record the condition when the daily allowance is exhausted.
FR-65: The system shall retry failed calls with an increasing delay on quota and transient server errors, up to a configured maximum number of attempts.
FR-66: Every run shall write exactly one summary record capturing its outcome, coverage, quota consumption and any error, including when the run fails.
FR-67: The system should raise an external notification when a run fails or when daily consumption exceeds a configured threshold.
FR-68: The system shall expose a derived feature view containing one row per video with its pre-publication features, horizon targets and target-quality flags.
FR-69: The system shall use a horizon as a training target only where the recorded quality flag marks it as usable.
FR-70: The system shall retain videos with fewer than thirty days of history, leaving the unavailable horizons absent rather than excluding the video.
FR-71: The system shall exclude live broadcasts and rows with no usable target from training.
FR-72: The system shall record the number of rows removed at each selection stage and the number of usable rows per horizon.
FR-73: The system shall apply outlier removal on a transformed scale and shall record what was removed.
FR-74: The system shall not admit as a feature any value derived from the video's own post-publication performance or from the performance of its contemporaries.
FR-75: The system shall divide data into training, validation and test portions by publication date, and shall not use random cross-validation.
FR-76: The system shall compute any target-derived encoding within the training portion only, after the split has been made.
FR-77: The system shall build and measure a naive category baseline, and a category-by-size-tier variant, before the forecasting model is evaluated.
FR-78: The system shall report proportional error as the headline metric, combined and per horizon, together with supporting error and variance-explained metrics, all on the real view-count scale.
FR-79: The system shall define success as a quantified reduction in proportional error relative to the measured baseline, consistent across all four horizons.
FR-80: The system shall perform an ablation study measuring the contribution of each feature group, and shall record the result.
FR-81: The system shall publish, with every released model, the encoding map, the ordered feature list, the shared preprocessing implementation, the metrics report and the training configuration.
FR-82: The system shall retrain and re-evaluate as further labelled data matures, and shall version each released model.
UR-01: A first-time user with no prior exposure to the system shall be able to complete a forecast request and interpret the result without training, documentation or assistance.
UR-02: The system shall require no user account, installation or configuration before a forecast can be requested.
UR-03: The forecast request shall be completable from a single screen, without navigation between steps.
UR-04: The system shall be verified against UR-01 by an informal usability check with a small group of representative users, in which the ability to reach an actionable forecast unaided is the pass condition.
UR-05: The system shall express forecasts, recommendations and error messages in everyday language, without statistical notation or model terminology.
UR-06: Where a numeric accuracy figure is shown, the system shall accompany it with a plain explanation of what it means and how it should be read.
UR-07: The system shall present each recommendation together with the historical pattern supporting it, phrased as an observation rather than as an instruction.
UR-08: The system shall require only those inputs that cannot be derived automatically, and shall derive all others from the supplied channel identifier and title.
UR-09: The system shall report an invalid input by identifying the field, stating what is wrong and stating what an acceptable value looks like.
UR-10: The system shall preserve entered values when reporting an error or presenting a result, so that a single field can be amended and the request repeated.
UR-11: The system shall indicate that a request is in progress whenever a response is not immediate.
UR-12: The system shall accept, store, display and process text in Sinhala, Tamil and Latin scripts, and mixtures of them, without character loss or corruption.
UR-13: The system shall render multi-script text legibly in every view in which titles appear.
UR-14: The dashboard should be usable on a mobile-sized viewport as well as on a desktop browser.
REL-01: The dashboard shall be available during normal use without a guaranteed continuous availability level; scheduled and unscheduled interruptions are acceptable and are not considered failures of the system.
REL-02: The collection pipeline shall run to its schedule without manual intervention, and any run that does not complete shall be visible in the run log.
REL-03: The system shall record the proportion of scheduled collection runs that complete successfully and the resulting rate of missing observations, and shall report these as measures of pipeline completeness.
REL-04: The project shall take the measures needed to prevent the hosted scheduler from disabling the collection workflow through prolonged repository inactivity.
REL-05: All writes to the engagement history shall be idempotent on the natural key of video and age, such that repetition neither duplicates nor fails.
REL-06: A run that fails part-way shall leave the database in a consistent state and shall be safely repeatable.
REL-07: The warehouse shall be backed up automatically, and the backup shall be verified as restorable.
REL-08: The system shall handle videos that become unavailable after publication, and responses that omit expected fields, without failing the enclosing run.
REL-09: The failure or unavailability of the title-scoring service shall degrade the forecast rather than prevent it.
REL-10: The failure or unavailability of the channel-statistics lookup shall degrade the forecast rather than prevent it, where the creator can be informed of the degradation.
REL-11: Where a forecast cannot be produced at all, the system shall state that plainly and shall not present an estimated or placeholder figure in its place.
REL-12: Exhaustion of the daily API allowance shall cause collection to stop cleanly and be logged, and shall not corrupt data already collected.
REL-13: Collected engagement values shall faithfully reproduce those reported by the source at the time of observation, with no interpolation or smoothing at ingest.
REL-14: The system shall record, for each horizon label, the deviation between the observation used and the exact horizon boundary, and shall mark the label unusable where that deviation is unacceptable.
REL-15: The published model shall achieve a quantified reduction in proportional error relative to the measured naive baseline, consistent across all four horizons.
REL-16: Reported accuracy shall be measured on data withheld from training and shall be published per horizon as well as combined.
REL-17: No critical defect, as defined above, shall be present in a released version.
REL-18: The project shall record measured availability, run success rate and observed failure and repair times during operation, so that numeric reliability targets can be set in a subsequent revision of this specification.
PERF-01: The system shall acknowledge a submitted forecast request immediately and shall display a clear indication that processing is in progress until a result or an error is shown.
PERF-02: No fixed maximum response time is required of the prediction path; correctness and completeness take precedence over latency.
PERF-03: The system shall apply a timeout to each external service call and shall proceed with that input treated as missing rather than waiting indefinitely.
PERF-04: A scheduled collection run should complete within its scheduling interval so that consecutive runs do not overlap.
PERF-05: The system shall serve concurrent forecast requests at the modest volume characteristic of occasional individual use without degradation of correctness.
PERF-06: Live forecast requests shall consume a negligible share of the daily API allowance relative to background collection.
PERF-07: The system shall monitor warehouse storage growth against the available allocation and shall make the measured growth rate visible to the maintainers.
PERF-08: Model training shall be feasible on commodity hardware without specialised acceleration.
PERF-09: The prediction path shall execute within the memory and runtime limits of the target serverless environment.
SEC-01: API keys, database credentials and any other secret shall be supplied through the deployment platform's secret mechanism and read from the environment at run time.
SEC-02: No secret shall be committed to source control, embedded in client-side code, written to a log, or included in any response returned to a browser.
SEC-03: Every call to an external service shall be made from server-side code, so that no external-service credential is ever present in the browser.
SEC-04: External API keys shall be restricted to the specific services they are required for.
SEC-05: All communication between the browser and the system, and between the system and external services, shall use encrypted transport.
SEC-06: The system shall require no user account, authentication or personal information in order to produce a forecast, and shall not collect personal data from creators.
SEC-07: The system shall store only publicly available video and channel information.
SEC-08: The system shall rate-limit forecast requests so that automated or repeated use cannot exhaust the daily API allowance relied upon by the collection pipeline.
SEC-09: The system shall validate and constrain all input received from the browser before it is used in an external call or a database operation.
SEC-10: Error messages returned to the browser shall not disclose internal implementation detail, stack traces or configuration.
SUP-01: Python code shall follow the language's standard style guide, with a consistent naming convention applied across scripts, modules and database objects.
SUP-02: The repository shall follow a documented structure separating collection scripts, database definitions, model code and the dashboard application.
SUP-03: Dependencies shall be declared with pinned versions so that an environment can be reconstructed exactly.
SUP-04: Feature preparation shall be implemented once in a shared module used by both the training pipeline and the prediction service, and shall not be duplicated.
SUP-05: The project shall include an automated test asserting that a known training row passed through the serving path reproduces its training feature vector exactly.
SUP-06: Any new model input shall be added to the shared derived feature view rather than computed ad hoc in analysis code.
SUP-07: Every training run shall record its hyperparameters, split boundary, row-filter counts and random seed, such that the run can be reproduced.
SUP-08: Every released model shall be versioned and accompanied by its metrics report.
SUP-09: Every scheduled run shall write a summary record sufficient to diagnose a failure without direct inspection of the database.
SUP-10: Configuration and credentials shall be externalised from code so that the system can be redeployed to a new environment without modification of source.
SUP-11: The repository shall contain a README describing setup, required secrets, how to run each script, and the known operational risks of the scheduled workflow.
SUP-12: The data collection methodology shall be documented in sufficient detail for the dataset to be extended or reproduced by future work.
SUP-13: Known limitations, including the scoping assumption on viewer country and the absence of prediction intervals, shall be documented in a form visible to users of the system.
DC-01: Every component of the system shall operate within the free tier of the service hosting it; no component shall require paid hosting, compute, storage or API access.
DC-02: The system shall be designed so that exceeding a free-tier limit degrades or halts a background function rather than incurring a charge.
DC-03: The collection pipeline shall be implemented in Python 3.11 or later.
DC-04: Persistent data shall be stored in a managed PostgreSQL database.
DC-05: Scheduled collection shall be executed by a hosted CI workflow rather than by a self-managed server.
DC-06: The forecasting model shall be a gradient-boosted decision tree model unless a documented evaluation shows an alternative to be superior on the same held-out data.
DC-07: No model feature shall depend on information generated at or after the video's publication timestamp.
DC-08: No feature shall rank or compare a video against its contemporaneously published peers.
DC-09: Backward-looking category and channel aggregates shall be computed over a period ending strictly before the video's publication timestamp.
DC-10: A video's age shall be computed from its stored publication timestamp on every occasion on which it is required.
DC-11: The stored data model shall make the publication-anchored age the key of the engagement history, so that the invariant is structurally enforced.
DC-12: All timestamps shall be stored in UTC; conversion to Sri Lanka local time shall occur only at the feature-engineering and presentation layers.
DC-13: No feature quantifying divisiveness, communal or ethnic provocation, controversy potential or misleading-claim strength shall be computed, stored or exposed anywhere in the system.
DC-14: The recommendation layer shall generate guidance only from sustainable levers: clarity of framing, genuine interest, timing, duration and format.
DOC-01: Each input field shall carry a concise in-context explanation of what it is and why it is needed.
DOC-02: The system shall provide a short methodology and limitations page, in plain language, describing what the forecast is based on, the scoping assumption on viewer country, and the factors the model cannot observe.
DOC-03: The system shall provide a worked example showing a completed request and its interpretation.
DOC-04: The system shall provide a glossary of any term a non-technical creator may not recognise.
DOC-05: Help content shall be reachable from the forecast screen without losing entered values.
FR-83: The system shall not incorporate any component requiring purchase, subscription or paid licence.
FR-84: The system shall observe the licence and attribution terms of every open-source component it incorporates.
IF-01: The system shall present a browser-based user interface comprising a forecast request view, a result view, an accuracy view and a methodology and limitations view.
IF-02: The user interface shall visually distinguish required from optional inputs.
IF-03: The user interface shall expose no administrative, pipeline or database function.
IF-04: The user interface should meet recognised web accessibility guidance for contrast, keyboard operation and form labelling.
IF-05: The system shall define no hardware interface of its own.
IF-06: The user interface shall operate on a current desktop or mobile web browser with JavaScript enabled.
IF-07: The system shall interface with the external data API using its documented request format and shall use batched calls wherever the API supports them.
IF-08: The system shall exchange structured data with external services in a documented machine-readable format and shall validate every response before use.
IF-09: The system shall not automate retrieval from any service whose terms prohibit it.
IF-10: The model layer shall consume warehouse data exclusively through the derived feature view, which constitutes the interface between the collection tier and the model tier.
IF-11: All browser-to-system communication shall use asynchronous HTTP requests over TLS.
IF-12: All system-to-external-service communication shall use HTTPS.
IF-13: Database connections from scheduled jobs shall be made through a transaction-mode connection pooler over TLS.
IF-14: The pipeline shall expose no inbound network interface.
DB-01: The system shall use a relational database as its single persistent authoritative store.
DB-02: The database shall hold the channel roster, video records, engagement observations, title tone scores, the quota ledger and a summary record per pipeline run.
DB-03: The database shall expose a derived view presenting one row per video with its pre-publication features, horizon targets and target-quality flags.
DB-04: The engagement history shall be keyed such that each video has at most one authoritative observation per publication-anchored day, and writes shall be idempotent on that key.
DB-05: A video's publication timestamp shall be stored as the source of truth for every age calculation.
DB-06: Title tone scores shall be stored once per video rather than repeated across that video's observations.
DB-07: All timestamps shall be stored in UTC.
DB-08: The database shall accommodate videos with partial horizon coverage as a normal state.
DB-09: The database shall be backed up automatically, and storage growth shall be monitored against the available allocation.
DB-10: Connections from short-lived scheduled jobs shall be made through a transaction-mode pooler.
DB-11: The database shall record the source of each engagement observation, distinguishing automated collection from manually imported backfill.
DB-12: Retention of collected data shall comply with the data source's developer policies, and records for videos that become unavailable shall be marked rather than silently retained as current.
LEG-01: The system shall comply with the data source's API terms of service and developer policies, including their provisions on storage, retention, display and attribution.
LEG-02: The system shall display any attribution required by the terms under which it accesses third-party data.
LEG-03: The system shall not automate retrieval from any service whose terms prohibit it.
LEG-04: The system shall observe the licence and notice requirements of every open-source component it incorporates.
LEG-05: The system shall display a clear statement that the forecast is an estimate and not a guarantee of performance, in a position where a user will see it alongside the result.
LEG-06: The system shall not collect, store or process personal data belonging to users of the dashboard.
LEG-07: The collected dataset shall not be redistributed except as the source's terms permit.
STD-01: This specification shall conform to the organisation prescribed by IEEE Std 830-1998 as adapted by the project's SRS template.
STD-02: The system shall use UTF-8 character encoding end to end.
STD-03: The system shall use TLS 1.2 or later for all network communication.
STD-04: All stored timestamps shall use UTC in the standard date and time representation.
STD-05: The dashboard should conform to WCAG 2.1 level AA guidance for contrast, keyboard operation and form labelling.
